speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have generalized fatigue, mild fever, abdominal pain, and nausea. To narrow down the cause, have you noticed any changes in your urine color or stool appearance recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old female. The patient describes a 3-week history of generalized fatigue, mild fever, abdominal pain, and nausea. She recalls attending the state fair over a month ago where she tried various regional foods. Recently, she has observed the darkening of her urine, which she believes is due to inadequate water intake. She has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your diabetes and the dark urine, have you also noticed yellowing of your skin or eyes, or any clay-colored stools? REQUEST TEST: Liver function panel (LFTs), Bilirubin, Urinalysis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Liver Function Panel (LFTs): AST 488 U/L, ALT 798 U/L, Alkaline Phosphatase 72 U/L. Bilirubin Total: 3.6 mg/dL, Bilirubin Direct: 2.4 mg/dL. Urinalysis: Dark urine observed, consistent with elevated bilirubin.

text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and mild fever. I also have Abdominal pain, Nausea, Dark urine.
